goals.description: Stage 8 — sync serving evaluates the policy (authEnforcement)
pollSyncEnvelopes decides per poll instead of asking the host tables which whole documents to drop (resolvers.ts:1065 forbiddenIds)
Withhold whole outbox entries only — a partial run applies as though complete, because the receiver renumbers and validates no hashes
Hold a refused entry, never consume it — today it is marked fully delivered and trimmed, irreversibly, by whichever subject polled
Never withhold the auth and document scopes — they are what a replica folds to reach the origin's decision
Intersect the policy verdict with the host's existing check, never union — this is what makes stage 8 safe before the migration
Bind a channel to the address that created it and refuse a poll under a different one, since the subject is per poll and may be absent

Exit test: a peer converges on one granted scope, keeps auth+document, raises no dead letter, and backfills when the grant widens

notes.note: This is the hard blocker for rollout: nothing in production has ever emitted INITIALIZE_AUTH, so every document's policy is uninitialized and an uninitialized policy allows everything.

goals.description: Stage 9 — migrate the host permission tables into grants (no flag)
Build the migration: one INITIALIZE_AUTH per document through the executor, using the five-step ordered grant list (grants cannot be written as rows)
Refuse and report what has no faithful translation — inherited protection, over-cap documents, owner-less documents; drop node-local admins
Dry run writes nothing and reports exactly what it cannot express; a real run is idempotent by skipping an initialized auth scope
Runbook: one replica with auth writes quiesced — two writers produce tied timestamps the monotonic rule refuses and nothing repairs
Exit test: on a fixture holding every construct, the read gate and the tables answer identically after migration and preflight:auth reports clean
Stage 10 — retire the permission tables (authEnforcement)
Stop consulting the tables on the read path: subgraph read helpers, per-item list filters, subscription predicates, attachment gate, stage-8 intersection
Listings synthesize a document-level verdict — readable if any gated scope is — or every id, slug and access list stays enumerable
Keep the host default on the receiving write door as a local refusal that never records a denial into any history
Boot assertion: refuse to start with authEnforcement on against untranslated rows, unless the host closes by default
Delete authorization.service.ts and document-permission.service.ts once nothing reads them; the node-operator check stays
Exit test: the read-denial suites pass against the migrated fixture, restated to what the caller received; an unmigrated store fails to boot
Rollout — turn the four flags on, fleet by fleet

goals.description: Make the policy reachable — authoring, query surface, UI, docs (scope unconfirmed: the spec never mentions these)
No way to author a policy at all: no mutation, CLI, SDK helper or UI for INITIALIZE_AUTH / SET_GRANT / REMOVE_GRANT / MOVE_GRANT outside tests
The auth subgraph answers only from the old tables — no query for a document's grants, policy version, creator, or 'may I?'
No authorization React hooks exist; permission-aware UI must query the subgraph directly, and the read gate's predicate is async so a hook needs a caching story
reactor-group ships a document model with no editor — group membership can only be changed programmatically
Write the auth-scope academy docs, and rewrite the Authorization pages and switchboard Auth.md that stage 10 makes wrong
No e2e coverage: every stage exit test is a cross-process scenario unit tests cannot reach
The knowledge vault holds no note on grants, conditions or groups — its auth cluster describes the pre-scope model
Known limitations carried forward
Extract the write cache's twice-duplicated upgrade-boundary segmentation — the prerequisite for an upgrade-aware walk
